behavior_items: The reproducer exercises GCC's handling of an enum type that is first introduced by a forward declaration and later completed with a definition carrying the packed attribute. The key scenario is not ordinary enum parsing, but type merging across an incomplete-to-complete enum transition where layout-affecting attributes must remain consistent.

A forward-declared enum creates an initial placeholder type node for the enum tag name. When the later full enum definition is seen, GCC is expected to complete or merge that existing type node rather than silently creating an incompatible second variant for the same source-level type.

The packed attribute on an enum affects representation details of the enumeral type, specifically the underlying mode/size choice and the TYPE_PACKED property recorded on the tree node. Because packed changes ABI-relevant layout information, it must be treated consistently across all variants or redeclarations of the type.

The failure indicates that GCC ends up with two internal enumeral_type nodes for the same enum name fmt_type that are nearly the same but differ in TYPE_PACKED-related state. The diagnostic explicitly says 'type variant differs by TYPE_PACKED', which means GCC's internal variant/canonical-type machinery found two versions of what should be one compatible type, but one is marked packed and the other is not consistently so.

The dumped internal types show both nodes carry the packed attribute in their attribute list, yet they still differ in core flags: one appears as 'unsigned packed QI' while the other appears as 'readonly unsigned QI'. This suggests the bug is not merely missing parsing of __attribute__((packed)), but inconsistent propagation of structural flags when building or completing the enum type.

Both internal enum nodes use unsigned char / QI mode as their underlying representation, so the reproducer is not about disagreement over final byte width. Instead, it is about GCC's type identity rules: two enum variants with matching visible attributes still disagree in internal bookkeeping, enough to violate verify_type invariants.

The crash occurs during LTO compilation with -flto, specifically in the IPA pass '*free_lang_data'. That pass strips front-end-specific language data after earlier stages have already built and referenced the type graph. LTO and checking builds are good at exposing latent type inconsistencies because they traverse, canonicalize, and verify type nodes more aggressively than a plain non-LTO compile might.

The backtrace shows verify_type in tree.cc detects the inconsistent type variant and aborts with an internal compiler error. This means the reproducer reaches a compiler self-check rather than user-facing semantic rejection. In other words, GCC recognizes an impossible internal state after accepting the source far enough to enter interprocedural cleanup.

The presence of canonical-type differences in the dump also matters: one enum node's canonical type points at the base integer type while the other points elsewhere. That is another sign that the type completion/reuse path for the forward declaration is producing a mismatched relationship between the enum's main variant, its canonical type, and its packedness.

This reproducer therefore stresses redeclaration compatibility logic for tagged enums combined with attribute application timing. The important compiler behavior is: parse incomplete enum tag, later apply packed on completion, merge attributes and main-variant state, then verify consistency under LTO. GCC mishandles one of these transitions and leaves an invalid pair of related enum types.

Because the ICE happens in a checking build's verification path, the underlying front-end bug likely exists even when the compiler does not crash. In non-checking or different build configurations, the same source could potentially lead to silent type corruption, missed diagnostics, or ABI inconsistencies rather than an immediate ICE.

The bug report title captures the minimal trigger precisely: 'forward declaration of enum followed by packed on the enum type'. That combination is the essential reducer. The reproducer is not about enum values, control flow, or code generation logic; it is narrowly about type declaration order, attribute attachment, and internal type-node consistency.
test_behavior_analysis.summary: The reproducer triggers a GCC internal compiler error by forward-declaring an enum and then later defining that same enum with the packed attribute. This exercises GCC's enum type completion and redeclaration-merging logic, especially the interaction between an incomplete enum tag and a later layout-affecting attribute. GCC incorrectly creates or preserves incompatible internal variants of the same enum type, which differ in TYPE_PACKED-related state even though they correspond to one source-level enum. Under -flto, the IPA free_lang_data pass calls verify_type, which detects the inconsistent type graph and aborts with 'type variant differs by TYPE_PACKED'. The core bug is therefore an internal type consistency failure in enum redeclaration/attribute handling, exposed during LTO verification rather than normal user semantic diagnostics.

test_failure_analysis.analysis: The common pattern is a redeclaration/merge failure for a tagged enum that transitions from an incomplete forward declaration to a completed definition with a layout-affecting attribute. The failure is not in enum value computation or code generation, but in GCC's internal type identity machinery for enum tree nodes. The observed dump shows two enumeral_type nodes for the same source-level enum tag fmt_type that should have been unified or completed consistently, but instead differ in TYPE_PACKED-related state and canonical/main-variant bookkeeping. Because packed changes ABI-relevant representation, GCC must propagate it uniformly when completing the previously forward-declared enum. The fact that both dumped nodes already carry the packed attribute list, yet verify_type still reports a TYPE_PACKED mismatch, strongly suggests a bug in structural flag propagation or variant construction rather than simple attribute parsing. The crash during IPA free_lang_data under -flto indicates that front-end type construction left an invalid type graph that later verification exposed when language-specific data was stripped and types were rechecked. So the likely defect area is C front-end enum redeclaration/completion logic together with generic tree type variant/canonical-type maintenance for enumeral types when attributes such as packed are attached after an initial forward declaration.
possible_causes: Bug in C front-end enum completion/redeclaration merging: when a forward-declared enum is later defined with __attribute__((packed)), GCC creates a second enumeral_type or fails to retrofit the existing incomplete type node, leaving incompatible packed vs non-packed state for the same tag.

Incorrect propagation of TYPE_PACKED from the parsed attribute list to the enum's main variant during incomplete-to-complete type transition, so the attribute is recorded textually but the core type flag/variant identity is not updated consistently.

Defect in build_distinct_type_copy / type variant construction for enumeral types, where applying packed to an enum redeclaration produces a variant that differs in forbidden structural fields instead of reusing or normalizing the existing main type.

Canonical-type maintenance bug for enums with late-applied attributes: the completed enum gets a mismatched TYPE_CANONICAL or TYPE_MAIN_VARIANT relationship, causing verify_type to compare two related enum nodes that differ by TYPE_PACKED.

Failure in attribute merging logic for tagged enum redeclarations: packed is treated as an attribute on one declaration path but as a structural type property on another, leading to divergence between TYPE_ATTRIBUTES and TYPE_PACKED.

LTO/IPA free_lang_data latent-type-corruption exposure: earlier front-end code leaves inconsistent enum variants, and the free_lang_data/type verification path fails because it does not preserve or reconcile packedness uniformly across enum variants after stripping language data.

Possible bug in enum stub creation for forward declarations: the placeholder enum type may be initialized with readonly/other default qualifiers or canonical links that are later copied into the completed type without synchronizing packedness, yielding the readonly-vs-packed discrepancy shown in the dump.

The spec consists of one dollar symbol for each specified variable bound, one asterisk for each unspecified variable bound, followed by at most one specification of the most significant bound of an ordinary array parameter. For ordinary arrays the specification is either the constant bound itself, or the space character for an array with an unspecified bound (the [] form). No "arg spec" is created for parameters of pointer types, making a distinction between T(*)[N] (or, equivalently, T[][N]) and the T[M][N] form, all of which have the same type and are represented the same, but only the last of which gets an "arg spec" describing the most significant bound M.

Wrap a SAVE_EXPR around EXPR, if appropriate. Do this to any expression which may be used in more than one place, but must be evaluated only once. Normally, expand_expr would reevaluate the expression each time. Calling save_expr produces something that is evaluated and recorded the first time expand_expr is called on it. Subsequent calls to expand_expr just reuse the recorded value. The call to expand_expr that generates code that actually computes the value is the first call *at compile time*. Subsequent calls at compile time* generate code to use the saved value. This produces correct result provided that *at run time* control always flows through the insns made by the first expand_expr before reaching the other places where the save_expr was evaluated. You, the caller of save_expr, must make sure this is so. Constants, and certain read-only nodes, are returned with no SAVE_EXPR because that is safe. Expressions containing placeholders are not touched; see tree.def for an explanation of what these are used for.

Subroutine of stabilize_reference; this is called for subtrees of references. Any expression with side-effects must be put in a SAVE_EXPR to ensure that it is only evaluated once. We don't put SAVE_EXPR nodes around everything, because assigning very simple expressions to temporaries causes us to miss good opportunities for optimizations. Among other things, the opportunity to fold in the addition of a constant into an addressing mode often gets lost, e.g. "y[i+1] += x;". In general, we take the approach that we should not make an assignment unless we are forced into it - i.e., that any non-side effect operator should be allowed, and that cse should take care of coalescing multiple utterances of the same expression should that prove fruitful.

Main entry point for the GIMPLE front end. This front end has three main personalities: - LTO (-flto). All the object files on the command line are loaded in memory and processed as a single translation unit. This is the traditional link-time optimization behavior. - WPA (-fwpa). Only the callgraph and summary information for files in the command file are loaded. A single callgraph (without function bodies) is instantiated for the whole set of files. IPA passes are only allowed to analyze the call graph and make transformation decisions. The callgraph is partitioned, each partition is written to a new object file together with the transformation decisions. - LTRANS (-fltrans). Similar to -flto but it prevents the IPA summary files from running again. Since WPA computed summary information and decided what transformations to apply, LTRANS simply applies them.
